layers.label: Core
layers.explanation: At roughly 15 million K and 250 billion atmospheres, hydrogen nuclei collide here hard enough to fuse into helium — the engine of the whole star.

layers.label: Radiative zone
layers.explanation: Energy crawls outward through this layer as light, constantly re-absorbed and re-emitted, taking tens of thousands of years to cross it.

layers.label: Convective zone
layers.explanation: The outer shell, where hot gas rises and cooled gas sinks in churning cells — like a pot of boiling water scaled up to a planetary scale.

layers.label: Photosphere
layers.explanation: The visible 'surface.' Its temperature for the Sun is about 5,772 K — the layer whose color tells us the star's temperature.

hotspots.label: Core — fusion furnace
hotspots.description: The star's engine. ~15 million K and 250 billion Earth-atmospheres squeeze hydrogen into helium, releasing the energy that props the star open.

hotspots.label: Radiative zone
hotspots.description: Energy moves photon by photon, absorbed and re-emitted in random directions, slowly leaking outward through this mid-layer.

hotspots.label: Convective zone
hotspots.description: The churning outer shell where hot gas rises and cooled gas sinks, like a pot of water boiling — and that churn is what makes the surface look grainy.

hotspots.label: Photosphere — visible surface
hotspots.description: The visible disk of the star. Its color acts as a thermometer: red near 3,000 K, yellow-white at 5,800 K like the Sun, blue-white above 10,000 K.

hotspots.label: Hydrostatic balance
hotspots.description: The tug of war behind a steady star — gravity pulling every layer inward, fusion pushing every layer outward, both forces summing to zero so the star holds its size.
hotspots.positionHint: A force-symbol emblem floating above the star

visualStyleNotes: Warm off-white sphere with a section cut away on the left to show three nested zones, following Anatomy Atelier's clean-3D look. Yellow-white photosphere, orange interior bands; the outer convective zone shows subtle boiling texture; two translucent arrows (inward golden, outward pale blue) float in balance above the star to depict hydrostatic equilibrium. Hotspots as glowing umber beads with soft labels, no cluttered overlays.
materialNotes: Core: emissive warm yellow-white, slight inner glow. Radiative zone: translucent amber. Photosphere: rough surface with faint granule texture. Use gentle ambient warm lighting so the model reads as a drawing rather than a photograph.
assetBrief: Procedural Three.js scene in the quasar app's space/stars folder: star sphere (cutaway on left third), layered zones, balanced in/out arrows, camera that frames the full sphere with auto-rotate. Hotspot bead radius ~0.14, picking raycast as in other scenes so toggling is consistent.
